Random effects can be added to any generalized linear model.
A **generalized linear mixed model** (GLMM)
adds random effects to the linear predictor,
so for a binary outcome with random intercepts,

$$
\logf{\frac{\pi_{ij}}{1 - \pi_{ij}}} = \tp{\vx_{ij}}\vb + \alpha_j,
\qquad
\alpha_j \siid \ndist{0, \sigma_\alpha^2}
$$ {#eq-glmm}

[@dobson4e, Chapter 11; @gelman2006data, Chapter 14].
Each group's odds are multiplied by $\expf{\alpha_j}$,
so about 95% of groups have odds within a factor of
$\expf{\pm 2\sigma_\alpha}$ of the odds for a typical group
[@rocke2021epi204].

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-cbpp}
#### Contagious bovine pleuropneumonia

The `cbpp` data in the `lme4` package [@bates2015lme4]
record the number of new cases of contagious bovine pleuropneumonia
in 15 herds of zebu cattle in Ethiopia,
each observed in up to four periods.
The herds are a sample of all herds,
so we model herd as a random effect and period as a fixed effect:

```{r}
#| label: cbpp-glmer
#| code-fold: show
cbpp_glmer <- glmer(
  cbind(incidence, size - incidence) ~ period + (1 | herd),
  family = binomial,
  data = cbpp
)
summary(cbpp_glmer)$coefficients
VarCorr(cbpp_glmer)
```

The estimated herd standard deviation is $\est\sigma_\alpha \approx 0.642$,
so about 95% of herds have odds of a new case between
$\expf{-2 \times 0.642} \approx 0.28$ and $\expf{2 \times 0.642} \approx 3.6$
times those of a typical herd.
Holding herd fixed,
the odds of a new case in period 4 are
$\expf{-1.58} \approx 0.21$ times the odds in period 1.
:::

The fixed-effect coefficients in a GLMM are **conditional** on the random effect:
they compare odds within the same group.
Because the logit link is nonlinear,
these coefficients are not the same as population-averaged odds ratios
[@dobson4e, Chapter 11].
